claims.text: Applying a MoS2-doped DLC nanocomposite coating to an HEA surface will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate relative to the untreated alloy.
The simultaneous friction and wear reductions will persist from room temperature to approximately 800 °C.
The untreated HEA exhibits high friction and wear because of its conventional surface properties.
MoS2 is a high-temperature-stable lubricious dopant suitable for the proposed service range.
The doped DLC coating will form a robust, adherent lubricious tribolayer on the HEA.
The tribolayer will retain its integrity and low-shear properties across temperature extremes up to about 800 °C.
The MoS2 component provides an inherent shear plane that reduces friction.
A nanocomposite coating can provide low friction and low wear under sliding contact.
The coating's nanocomposite structure will resist wear by mitigating adhesive and abrasive interactions between moving parts.
The DLC matrix will preserve the coating's tribological properties under thermal stress.
The coated alloy will show significant and sustained reductions in both coefficient of friction and wear rate over the full tested temperature range.
Temperatures above the stability threshold of the DLC or dopant may eliminate the coating's effectiveness through decomposition.
Highly oxidative environments may degrade the proposed coating.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction may depend on coating thickness, dopant concentration, and sliding conditions.
Failure to obtain statistically significant and consistent reductions in both friction and wear across the tested temperatures would falsify the hypothesis.
Coating decomposition or delamination under any tested condition would falsify the hypothesis.
